claim: Tokens are the smallest units a language model works with; they can be words, parts of words, characters or bytes. For Claude a token is roughly 3.5 English characters.
script_safe_wording: Before the model sees your question, the text is cut into tokens: words, pieces of words, sometimes single characters.

claim: Autoregressive language models are pretrained to predict the next word given the previous text; fine-tuning and RLHF then make them useful assistants.
script_safe_wording: At its core the model was trained to do one thing: predict the next word from the words before it.

claim: The context window is all the text the model can reference when generating a response, including the response itself; it is separate from the training data and acts as working memory.
script_safe_wording: The context window is the model's working memory: everything it can look at while writing the answer.

claim: Each turn's input contains all previous conversation history plus the current message; previous turns are preserved by being resent, not remembered.
script_safe_wording: Every time you send a message, the whole conversation is sent again. If something is not in that request, the model does not know it.

claim: As token count in the context grows, accuracy and recall degrade (context rot); more context is not automatically better.
script_safe_wording: More context is not always better. Give the model what matters, not everything.

claim: Temperature controls randomness in word choice; even at temperature 0 outputs are not fully deterministic.
script_safe_wording: A setting called temperature controls how adventurous the word choices are. Even at zero, the same question can get slightly different answers.

claim: Hallucinations are plausible yet incorrect statements; they arise from statistical pressure in pretraining and from training and evaluation that reward guessing over admitting uncertainty (Kalai, Nachum, Vempala, Zhang, OpenAI).
script_safe_wording: Researchers at OpenAI showed that models are trained and tested in ways that reward a confident guess over saying 'I don't know'. That is why a wrong answer can sound so sure.

claim: The model never executes anything on its own; with tools it emits a structured request, the application runs the operation, and the result flows back into the conversation.
script_safe_wording: On its own the model cannot check anything. With a tool, it asks, your software does the work, and the result goes back into its context.

claim: RAG passes documents retrieved from an external knowledge base into the context window at answer time; its effectiveness depends on the quality and relevance of that knowledge base.
script_safe_wording: Retrieval means fetching the right page from a checked knowledge base and putting it in front of the model before it answers. The answer is only as good as that base.

claim: The 2020 RAG paper (Lewis et al.) combined parametric and non-parametric memory and named provenance and updating world knowledge as open problems.
script_safe_wording: The idea of giving a model an outside library to read from was published in 2020, and showing where an answer comes from was named an open problem from the start.

claim: Cross-chat memory in Claude is a product feature: on by default for Free, Pro and Max, off by default on Team and Enterprise, and disabled in incognito chats.
script_safe_wording: When a chatbot seems to remember you, that is a feature the product added on top: it saves notes and puts them back into the context. The model itself remembers nothing between requests.

claim: OpenAI help article on tokens (rule of thumb about tokens per word).
script_safe_wording: Do not cite: page returned 403 and was not opened. A1 covers the point.

claim: September 2025: black pod hit Muyuka, Mbonge and Kumba after heavy rain since July; the South-West agriculture delegate advised farmers to intensify spraying; authorities cited late pruning, poor clearing and irregular fungicide application.
script_safe_wording: When the rains are heavy, black pod spreads fast, and the regional agriculture office tells farmers to keep up sanitation and spraying on schedule.

claim: Black pod in Cameroon is caused by Phytophthora megakarya; without control losses can reach 70-80 per cent; primary inoculum lives in the soil and spreads by rain splash; control combines cultural methods, fungicides and resistant material.
script_safe_wording: Black pod is caused by a water mould called Phytophthora; the species found in Cameroon and its neighbours, Phytophthora megakarya, is the most damaging one, and wet, humid weather wakes it up in the soil while rain splash carries it from pod to pod. (No loss percentages: the opened sources give none plainly.)

claim: Standard management: remove and destroy infected pods, harvest ripe pods regularly, prune and clear for airflow, apply copper-based (or metalaxyl plus copper) fungicide at intervals in the rainy season; typical recommendation 6-8 applications a year.
script_safe_wording: Sanitation comes first: harvest ripe pods regularly, take off and dispose of diseased and mummified pods and husks, prune and weed so light and air reach the canopy, then apply the fungicide the cooperative's agent schedules; research in Cameroon shows the cultural steps alone are not enough against this species, and less susceptible planting material helps over time. (No spray counts, intervals or product names.)

claim: Cameroon's Law 2003/003 of 21 April 2003 requires phytosanitary products to be registered or hold a provisional sales authorisation before distribution.
script_safe_wording: Under Cameroon's phytosanitary protection law, only registered products, or ones holding a provisional sales authorisation, may be imported, distributed, packaged or used, so a product a chatbot names may not be legal or available here.

claim: The FAO/WHO International Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management is a voluntary framework for everyone involved in producing, regulating and managing pesticides.
script_safe_wording: International guidance says pesticide use follows the label, the local registration and proper protection: three things a generic chatbot answer does not know.
